name: Python
certifications: PCPP1 - Certified Professional Python Programmer Level 1

beginner.summary: No programming experience assumed. Participants learn Python syntax, data structures, functions, files and testing, and finish with a working command-line tool.
prerequisites: Comfortable using a computer, a web browser and a text editor
Laptop with permission to install Python 3.12 and VS Code
outcomes: Write and run Python scripts using variables, conditions, loops and functions
Store and process data with lists, dictionaries, sets, files, CSV and JSON
Handle errors, debug failing code and write first unit tests with pytest
Build a small command-line application from a written requirement

subtopics: Running code in the REPL and from a .py file
Reading a traceback for a syntax error

Read a traceback to find a syntax or indentation error

intermediate.summary: For participants who already write Python scripts. Covers idiomatic Python, object-oriented design, testing, data, APIs, packaging and concurrency, ending with a tested REST service.
prerequisites: Writes Python scripts with functions, loops, lists and dictionaries without help
Has used pip, virtual environments and basic file handling
Laptop with Python 3.12, Git and permission to install packages
outcomes: Write idiomatic, typed, tested Python using classes, generators, decorators and context managers
Work with REST APIs, pandas and SQL databases from Python
Build, test and package a FastAPI service
Use concurrency and asyncio where they help, and explain when they do not

subtopics: enumerate() and zip() instead of index loops

advanced.summary: For working Python developers. Covers Python internals, performance, advanced concurrency, architecture, security, delivery and production operations, ending with a production-grade service.
prerequisites: At least one year writing production Python, including classes, tests and packaging
Has built or maintained a web API or data pipeline in Python
Comfortable with Git, the command line and Docker basics
outcomes: Explain Python internals and use them to diagnose memory and performance problems
Design maintainable, secure, observable Python services
Profile and optimise CPU, memory and I/O bottlenecks with measured results
Deliver and operate a containerised async service with CI/CD
